Using a one-loop finite-temperature potential with ring resummation, we follow a strongly supercooled transition at the few-TeV scale through nucleation, percolation, completion, and reheating. The leading-order friction diagnostic does not support a runaway wall, so sound waves dominate the gravitational-wave signal, with turbulence as a sub-leading contribution; the finite acoustic lifetime suppresses the peak. For the fast-wall reference case, the spectrum peaks at $f_{\rm peak}=0.611$ Hz with $h^2\Omega_{\rm GW,peak}=1.232\times10^{-11}$, in the deci-Hz band targeted by DECIGO and BBO. We present its dependence on the wall speed, renormalization scale, and thermal screening, together with a noise-only comparison for several proposed detector configurations.
item.dc:creator: Haotian Huangfu, Tianjun Li, Qi Sun, Rui Sun, Wenxing Zhang

item.title: Gamma classes, central connection matrices, and tt* geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.11338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review the gamma class of complex projective space, but from the point of view of topological-antitopological fusion. We deconstruct the central connection matrix which appears in the work of Dubrovin, Galkin-Golyshev-Iritani, and Cotti-Dubrovin-Guzzetti.
item.dc:creator: Martin A. Guest

item.title: The Fate of Collisional Neutrino Flavor Conversion: Fixed Points, Period Doubling, and Chaos
item.description: arXiv:2611.11351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Core-collapse supernovae and neutron star mergers are among the most energetic astrophysical events and promising sources of multimessenger signals. Their dynamics and nucleosynthesis depend sensitively on neutrino transport, yet the impact of neutrino flavor evolution in these dense environments remains poorly understood. Predicting the outcome of collisional flavor instability (CFI) remains a challenge, despite progress in local-relaxation methods for fast flavor conversion. Here we construct homogeneous collective-precession states with stationary flavor populations in two-flavor quantum kinetics with collisional relaxation. The method applies to arbitrary energy spectra and energy-dependent collision rates. Our numerical examples exhibit persistent oscillations and a period-doubling route to chaos. Even in these regimes, the stationary populations estimate the time-averaged flavor populations to within $10\%$ in our tests. These fixed points provide a physically motivated input for incorporating CFI into astrophysical simulations, with implications for neutrino heating and ejecta nucleosynthesis.
item.dc:creator: Jiabao Liu, Lucas Johns, Hiroki Nagakura

item.title: Anomalous charge conjugation and parity in (2+1)-dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.11454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a hydrostatic and first-order constitutive description of a mixed anomaly that involves $U(1)_Q$, $U(1)_F$, charge conjugation symmetry (acting only on $U(1)_Q$), and parity symmetry in $2+1$ dimensions. It is represented by a mutual Chern-Simons level $k_{QF}=\frac12 \,(\mathrm{mod}\ \mathbb Z)$. Adopting the already established multi-charge anomaly sector, we explicitly provide the information that this response is $odd$ under $\mathsf{C}$ and $\mathsf{P}$ symmetries separately, but $even$ under combined $\mathsf{CP}$ symmetry. We also provide a global inflow representative and compute the equilibrium cross-charge response which includes $\partial n_Q/\partial B_F=\partial n_F/\partial B_Q=1/4\pi \bmod 1/2\pi$. Using an analytic neutral-fluid example we show that this response is non-vanishing whereas the source-free hydrodynamic poles are invariant.
item.dc:creator: Sonali Patnaik, Rajeev Singh

item.title: A geometrical approach for obtaining exact analytical solutions for a scalar field in a one-dimensional dynamical cavity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The dynamical Casimir effect was first predicted by G. T. Moore in 1969, who considered a real scalar field inside a cavity with a moving mirror in ($1+1$)D, satisfying Dirichlet boundary conditions. Moore wrote the general solution for the field in terms of a function that satisfies a functional equation nowadays known as the Moore equation.In the literature, exact analytical solutions to the Moore equation form a rather small set, restricted to specific classes of laws of motion. Cole and Schieve (1995) developed a geometrical approach that yielded a general formula for the solution of the Moore equation for cavities initially at rest. However, its application has always been done through numerical calculations, and their approach has therefore long been regarded solely as a numerical method. In this work, we show that their method can also be employed as a powerful method for deriving exact analytical solutions, and show the applicability of this approach to deriving analytical solutions to the Moore equation. We obtain original exact analytical solutions for an expanding cavity with a uniformly moving mirror, a contracting cavity with a mirror that approaches the static one asymptotically, and, in addition, we recover the first analytical solution to the Moore equation for a resonant mirror motion, originally obtained by Law in 1994. Moreover, we extend the Cole-Schieve approach, showing that exact solutions can be constructed from any spacetime region where the Moore function has already been determined. We show that this extended geometrical approach allows us to expand the set of known analytical solutions to the Moore equation from the few classes of motion reported in the literature to an infinite set, as it enables the treatment of new classes of laws of motion obtained by combining those presented here with each other as well as with previously known classes of trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Maxwell F. de Ara\'{u}jo, Odemar Juli\~{a}o do N. Neto, Stanley S. Coelho, Jeferson Danilo L. Silva, Alessandra N. Braga, Danilo T. Alves

item.title: Projective symmetries and differential recursions for the large-$N$ Gross--Witten--Wadia and one-dimensional QCD matrix models
item.description: arXiv:2611.11670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compare the fixed-charge planar Gross--Witten--Wadia (GWW) model with source-free one-dimensional QCD at large $N$ and $N_f/N$ fixed. In both models the resolvent and one-cut condition give an algebraic equation for a derivative of the free energy: a quartic for GWW and a sextic for QCD. Finite-$N$ Toeplitz determinants independently check the selected QCD branch. Signed permutations of homogeneous parameter triples realize $S_4$; the resulting action on the algebraic branches and operator labels gives a common projective description of the two models. For QCD, the sextic yields a differential recurrence linking small-charge rows two apart. The same second-order PDE gives a finite-width column recursion that reconstructs the coefficient pyramid from its GWW boundary. A distinct boundary, obtained from the first resummed coefficient, is the Narayana triangle. A formally collapsed slice counts decorated bipartite plane trees and admits an exact symmetric product formula. The many-flavor scaling reduces the sextic to the quartic and retains transverse projective data: the QCD divided-difference triple coalesces at this boundary, whereas the limiting quartic satisfies the full standard GWW third-order system. We distinguish algebraic degree, mixed differential order, and fixed-parameter ordinary differential order throughout.
item.dc:creator: S. Voloshyn

item.title: Nonlinear Scalarization of Reissner-Nordstr\"om Black Holes in Scalar-Torsion-Maxwell Teleparallel Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.11686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the nonlinear scalarization of Reissner-Nordstr\"om black holes in scalar-torsion-Maxwell teleparallel gravity, in which the scalar field is nonminimally coupled to the Weitzenb\"ock invariant. We consider polynomial coupling functions that avoid tachyonic instabilities at the linear level, thereby exploring a scalarization mechanism driven by nonlinear effects. In the decoupling limit, we study the nonlinear evolution of finite-amplitude scalar perturbations and show that the inclusion of a sixth-order coupling term allows the scalar field to dynamically evolve toward nontrivial stationary configurations. This behavior can be understood in terms of the effective potential, which develops nontrivial local minima that provide a mechanism for nonlinear saturation. By numerically solving the fully coupled field equations, we construct asymptotically flat charged black hole solutions endowed with scalar hair. We classify these solutions according to the number of nodes in the scalar field profile, identifying multiple branches whose structure and multiplicity depend on the coupling parameters. We further show that the higher-order coupling progressively suppresses higher-node branches and characterize the scalar backreaction through deviations of the metric functions and the torsion scalar from the Reissner-Nordstr\"om background.
item.dc:creator: Joaqu\'in Robledo, Yerko V\'asquez, P. A. Gonz\'{a}lez

item.title: Measurements of $C\!P$ violation with charm hadrons at Belle and Belle II
item.description: arXiv:2611.11957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent searches for $C\!P$ violation in charm-hadron decays at Belle and Belle II are presented. The measurements cover $D^+_{(s)}\to\eta h^+$, $D\to\pi\pi$, $D^0\to K_S^0K_S^0$, and $D^0\to\pi^+\pi^-\pi^0$, together with the singly Cabibbo-suppressed baryon decays $\Xi_c^+\to\Sigma^+h^+h^-$ and $\Lambda_c^+\to ph^+h^-$, where $h=\pi,K$. The Belle II analyses use the Run~1 data sample of $428\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$, supplemented by $980\,\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of Belle data for the $K_S^0K_S^0$ measurements. We report preliminary results for the $\eta h^+$ modes, complementary tests of the isospin structure of $D\to\pi\pi$, and an application of inclusive charm-flavor tagging. The first individual decay-rate asymmetries in these three-body charmed-baryon modes also provide tests of $U$-spin symmetry. All reported asymmetries are consistent with $C\!P$ symmetry within the present precision.
item.dc:creator: Jaeyoung Kim (on behalf of the Belle II Collaboration)

item.title: Naturalness in the Past from a Time-Dependent Supersymmetry Scale
item.description: arXiv:2611.12363v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the possibility that electroweak naturalness may be epoch dependent. In no-scale supergravity, a rolling quintessence modulus can control the supersymmetry-breaking scale, allowing superpartners to be much lighter in the early universe while remaining heavy today. Fifth-force and varying-constant effects can be suppressed via correlated modular weights in the visible-sector K\"ahler metric and modulus-dependent superpotential Yukawa couplings, while radiative stability of the quintessence potential requires additional tuning of the field-dependent vacuum energy. The resulting effective theory has distinctive implications for early-universe phase transitions, relic abundances, and gravitational waves.
item.dc:creator: Tony Gherghetta, Kunio Kaneta, Wenqi Ke

item.title: Holomorphic integer-graded vertex operator superalgebras are purely even
item.description: arXiv:2611.12417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that a simple, self-contragredient, rational, $C_2$-cofinite, integer-graded holomorphic vertex operator superalgebra of CFT-type has zero odd part. We first show that a hypothetical nonzero odd part would be a simple current of categorical dimension $-1$ over a strongly rational pointed VOA with four simple modules. We then prove that every nonvacuum simple current of a strongly rational VOA has strictly positive lowest conformal weight. This leads to a contradiction with Dong-Jiao-Xu's theorem on the positivity of categorical dimension.
item.dc:creator: Chongying Dong, Kaiwen Sun, Haowu Wang

item.title: Direct product geometries in $n$-dimensional linear, quadratic, and conformal gravity
item.description: arXiv:2611.12483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct-product spacetimes offer a tractable route to exact solutions in gravity theories beyond general relativity. We study $n$-dimensional direct-product spacetimes of $(m_1+m_2)$, $(2+m)$, and $(2+\ldots+2)$ type in linear gravity, general pure quadratic-curvature gravity, and one of the recently proposed higher-dimensional extensions of conformal gravity, allowing the two-dimensional subspaces to have nonconstant curvature. We classify the resulting solution spaces and determine how the allowed geometries depend on the gravitational theory and, in quadratic gravity, on the curvature couplings. Metrics containing two-dimensional part(s) of nonconstant curvature are governed either by algebraic conditions on a curvature profile or, in one special class of quadratic gravity, by a differential equation. Relations governing metrics with only constant-curvature $m$-dimensional subspaces are purely algebraic. We further examine conformal relations to linear-gravity solutions, generalized Petrov types, and compatibility with electromagnetic sources. Particularly noteworthy is that standard static black-hole geometries are absent from the direct-product sector of the considered form of conformal gravity for $n>4$. Four- and six-dimensional cases are analyzed in detail, and explicit analytic solutions illustrating the resulting structure are presented whenever possible.
item.dc:creator: Petr Jizba, Tereza Lehe\v{c}kov\'{a}

item.title: Real-Time Path Integral Resurgence: Which Classical Path Contributes?
item.description: arXiv:2611.12510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Which complex classical paths contribute to a real-time Feynman path integral? Picard-Lefschetz theory answers this question with the intersection numbers of the thimbles, which are notoriously hard to compute in infinite dimensions. We show that resurgence provides a practical alternative. We compute the asymptotic series of the real and complex classical paths to high order, with Feynman diagrams and with a transport recursion for the cumulants, and read off the adjacency of the classical paths from the divergent tails of the series with Borel-Pad\'e methods. The South-East rule then turns adjacency into relevance. For a particle meeting a Rosen-Morse barrier, we identify the relevant complex classical paths in front of and behind the barrier, including the complex path that carries quantum tunnelling, follow ordinary and higher-order Stokes phenomena as the final point moves, and verify the predictions with the exact propagator. The resummed series reproduce the propagator with exponential accuracy. Finally, we outline how the expansion extends to relativistic path integrals governed by a Hamiltonian constraint.
item.dc:creator: Job Feldbrugge

item.title: Pentagon Functions for Two-Loop Leading-Colour $pp\to t\bar{t}H$ Amplitudes with a Light-Quark Loop
item.description: arXiv:2611.12661v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a basis of special functions and an efficient numerical implementation for the planar two-loop master integrals that enter the leading-colour amplitudes for $pp\to t\bar{t}H$ with a closed light-quark loop. We provide analytic results for the special functions at transcendental weight one and two in terms of logarithms and dilogarithms, while higher weights are evaluated as one-fold integrals. We focus on the nested roots that arise, studying their analytic structure on the physical region and constructing numerically stable representations of letters and $\mathrm{d}\log$ forms that involve them. We find that a number of $\mathrm{d}\log$ forms have an antiderivative that cannot be represented by a single logarithm over the physical region and tackle them numerically with adaptive Chebyshev approximation. We implement the functions in \texttt{C++} as an extension of the \texttt{PentagonFunctions++} library. We study the performance of our implementation over physical phase-space points and find that the evaluation is accurate and fast enough for phenomenological application. This provides an important building block for NNLO studies of $t\bar{t}H$ production at the LHC.
item.dc:creator: Simone Devoto, Manfred Kraus, Ben Page

item.title: Thermodynamics of Kerr-Newman-Bertotti-Robinson black holes from background subtraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.12683v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The non-asymptotic flatness of charged rotating black holes immersed in the Bertotti-Robinson magnetic field causes the ambiguity in the gauge choice for the time generator and the horizon electric potential. By using the newly established form of the integrability condition together with the gauge choice for the asymptotically flat charged rotating black holes as the initial condition, we have found that the gauge can be uniquely fixed. With this fixed gauge, we further obtain the mass and angular momentum by the background subtraction method with the Minkowski spacetime as the reference spacetime. As a result, not only is the first law of black hole thermodynamics automatically satisfied, but also both the CR relation and the Smarr formula are obeyed.
item.dc:creator: Chang-Xu Yan, Zili Mou, Yu Tian, Hongbao Zhang

item.title: A possible signature of neutrino spin precession in the J-PARC muon $g-2$ experiment
item.description: arXiv:2611.12749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We examine a possible signature of the neutrino angular-momentum contribution to the muon magnetic anomaly measurement in the J-PARC E34 experiment. In previous papers we argued that the angular momentum carried by the unobserved neutrino pair may leave an uncertainty in the anomaly inferred from the time modulation of detected positrons. At Fermilab the highly relativistic muons make the forward-emission approximation suitable for this estimate. The lower muon momentum at J-PARC requires the decay kinematics to be treated explicitly. We integrate the longitudinal momentum of the neutrino pair using the positron energy distribution and asymmetry derived from the theoretical weak-decay spectrum, and the same event-counting weight $N(E)A(E)$ is employed for both experiments. For positron energies between $1.5$ and $2.9$ GeV at Fermilab and between $200$ and $275$ MeV at J-PARC, the proposed correction is smaller at J-PARC by $0.415\pm0.176$ ppm, when the most optimistic E34 precision is assumed. The expected difference amounts to $2.36$ standard deviations if the future measurement is centred on this value. The calculation thus identifies an experimental comparison which may test the proposed effect independently of the hadronic contribution to the Standard Model prediction. We also examine the possibility of testing the effect by comparing measurements at two different muon momenta. With a fixed positron energy threshold of 200 MeV, the maximum sensitivity is obtained at a muon beam energy of 245 MeV. The predicted difference relative to the nominal J-PARC configuration has significance of $4.88\sigma$ for the most optimistic experimental sensitivity.
item.dc:creator: S. Carneiro, F. C. Sobrinho

item.title: Quality time in extra dimensions: axion quality and radion cosmology
item.description: arXiv:2611.12765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher-form symmetries can protect extra-dimensional axions, but additional symmetry breaking can still spoil the solution to the strong CP problem. We focus on electrically charged matter and magnetic gauging in a five-dimensional circle compactification where the axion arises from an Abelian gauge field and the radius is dynamical. We discuss two mechanisms for stabilising the radius/radion using Casimir energy from fields neutral under the Abelian gauge field, with and without an additional periodic scalar winding around the compact circle. Both admit Minkowski and de Sitter minima. At the Minkowski minima (with radion masses of $100$--$170\,\mathrm{TeV}$), electrically charged matter induces a residual strong CP angle of order $10^{-17}$ and shifts the radius negligibly. Magnetic gauging remains compatible after including its additional degree of freedom in the Casimir spectrum, provided its coupling is sufficiently small. We observe that increasing the radius suppresses charged-matter breaking relative to QCD but increases magnetic breaking contribution. We also determine the radion decay channels, including the graviphoton, and study reheating from a possible radion-dominated era without scalar winding or magnetic gauging. For a non-minimal Higgs-curvature coupling $\xi=7$, the visible-sector reheating temperature is about $85\,\mathrm{MeV}$ with a dark-radiation contribution of $\Delta N_{\rm eff}\approx0.02$. The entropy released during radion decay dilutes the axion abundance, allowing axions with $f_a=10^{14}\,\mathrm{GeV}$ and an initial misalignment angle $\vartheta_i\approx0.43$ to account for the entire observed dark matter abundance. For the same decay constant, reproducing this abundance in radiation domination requires $\vartheta_i\approx0.065$.
item.dc:creator: Falguni Biswas, Yeshan Juberi, Ahmed Rakin Kamal

item.title: The structure of the pion at large $N_c$
item.description: arXiv:2611.12771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute the pion quark momentum fraction in the large-$N_c$ limit using the Twisted Eguchi-Kawai (TEK) reduced model. Gauge configurations for different values of the lattice spacing are generated with the pure-gauge TEK action, while the pion correlators are computed for different quark masses with maximally twisted mass fermions. The bare matrix element corresponding to the quark momentum fraction is obtained using the Feynman-Hellmann method, and we use perturbative renormalization factors to connect to the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme at $2\,\mathrm{GeV}$. A global analysis at several lattice spacings, pion masses, and values of $N_c$ yields $\langle x\rangle_q^{\overline{\mathrm{MS}}}(2\,\mathrm{GeV}) = 0.267(105)$ at the physical pion mass in the large-$N_c$ limit. This value is significantly smaller than existing $N_c=3$ determinations from phenomenology and lattice QCD, indicating that, in the large-$N_c$ limit, the pion's light-cone momentum is carried predominantly by gluons.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Zhu, Fernando Romero-L\'opez, Phiala E. Shanahan

item.title: Gravitational waves and the exit from de Sitter in Inflation without an Inflaton
item.description: arXiv:2611.12772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), second-order de Sitter (dS) gravitons generate primordial curvature as the Coulomb-type potential of their gradient stress. Each pair contributes $(p/k)^2$, yielding exponential enhancement over the contributing e-folds. With exact Bunch-Davies evolution, this solution satisfies all four scalar second-order Einstein equations in pure dS. The retarded transverse-traceless solution instead has a UV kernel of order unity, $(k/p)^2$ below the scalar kernel, and a one-loop correction $\Delta^2_{h,2}/\Delta^2_h\simeq0.04\,\Delta^2_h$. Its source acts before internal freeze-out, but oscillatory cancellations prevent tensor enhancement. We evolve the curvature through a smooth exit into radiation domination. Conserved curvature resides on the vacuum-decay hypersurface. A global depletion clock holds each scale on zero-shear time for $N_{\rm w}$ e-folds after horizon exit before local release, giving all scales equal enhancement. Energy-momentum conservation feeds the depleted vacuum energy into a non-vacuum sector, modeled as radiation. Deep in radiation domination, $\Delta^2_\zeta=c_w\Delta_h^4e^{N_{\rm w}}/20$, with clock-dependent $c_w$, $n_s-1=-4\epsilon$, and $n_T=-2\epsilon$. The spectrum is adiabatic and Gaussian; super-horizon $\zeta$ is conserved to better than $10^{-4}$, and changing the adiabatic exit fluid alters it by less than $0.2\%$. A direct radiation exit requires $31\lesssim N_{\rm w}\lesssim50$, or $3\times10^{-6}\lesssim r\lesssim0.036$. At interferometer frequencies, $\Omega_{\rm GW}h^2\simeq2\times10^{-21}$--$3\times10^{-17}$, accessible to BBO for $r\gtrsim0.01$ and ultimate DECIGO for $r\gtrsim10^{-5}$; CMB B-mode searches probe $r\gtrsim10^{-3}$. Above $k_{\rm end}e^{-N_{\rm w}}$, the scalar spectrum steepens to $k^{-1}$, suppressing $\mu$-distortions for sharp release when $N_{\rm w}\gtrsim45$.
item.dc:creator: Daniele Bertacca, Raul Jimenez, Sabino Matarrese, Mariam Abdelaziz, Marisol Traforetti

item.title: An efficient classical algorithm for OTOCs in chaotic quantum dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.12773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating out-of-time-ordered correlators (OTOCs) in individual instances of random quantum circuits has been proposed as a candidate for verifiable quantum advantage, and demonstrated to be hard for conventional classical algorithms such as tensor networks and Monte Carlo. Using insights from quantum chaos, we develop and implement a polynomial-time classical algorithm for the four-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and the eight-point ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in typical instances of one-dimensional (1D) quantum circuits. Our results demonstrate average-case classical tractability of estimating OTOCs in the sensitive regime where circuit-to-circuit fluctuations are large. Our algorithm organizes the OTOC into a rapidly converging series, where the leading term includes contributions from histories within permutation degrees of freedom in the replicated Hilbert space, and subleading terms arise from excursions outside this space. Although chaos is often viewed as an insurmountable barrier to classical simulation, our algorithm exploits a form of dephasing caused by chaos, which suppresses the subleading terms. We provide strong theoretical and numerical evidence to support this suppression. Further, we demonstrate that practical implementations of our algorithm estimate ${\rm OTOC}^{(1)}$ and ${\rm OTOC}^{(2)}$ in 1D circuits with high accuracy, achieving higher signal-to-noise ratio at larger circuit depths compared to recent 2D experiments by Google. Extending our algorithm to higher dimensions, and resolving the status of quantum advantage in 2D OTOCs, remain open problems.
item.dc:creator: Yunchao Liu, Yihui Quek, Shreya Vardhan, Tianci Zhou

item.title: Property F implies weak integrality for non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.12836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every non-degenerate pivotal braided fusion category with property F is pseudo-unitary and weakly integral. In particular, every modular category with property F is weakly integral. Neither sphericality nor pseudo-unitarity is assumed. Passing to the Drinfeld centre extends the result to degenerate categories whose dimensions are positive on the intersection of the M\"uger centre with the adjoint subcategory; these include every braided fusion category with a pseudo-unitary Galois conjugate. Physically, the result connects the arithmetic of topological orders to the computational power of anyon braiding: non-integer squared total quantum dimension guarantees infinite braid group images, a necessary condition for universal quantum computation.
item.dc:creator: Justin Asher, Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham

item.title: Scalar quasinormal modes of the exact spinning Morris--Thorne wormhole
item.description: arXiv:2611.12838v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the quasinormal modes (QNMs) of a minimally coupled massless scalar field on the exact spinning Morris-Thorne wormhole. The problem is posed on the complete two-ended geometry, whose asymptotic rest frames rotate relative to each other. After extracting the axis behaviour and the outgoing phases at both infinities, we compactify the radial coordinate and construct a quadratic eigenvalue problem by two-dimensional Chebyshev collocation. The analytic background yields exact constraints on the spectrum. At fixed azimuthal number $m$, the frequencies $\widehat{\omega}=r_0\omega$ are mirror symmetric about $\operatorname{Re}\widehat{\omega}=3\pi jm/2$, where $r_0$ is the throat radius and $j=J/r_0^2$ is the dimensionless angular momentum. Each multipole family depends on $m$ and $j$ only through $mj$ and three angular Chebyshev polynomials represent exactly the multipoles $L=|m|,|m|+1,|m|+2$. A conserved flux confines nonthreshold real quasinormal frequencies to the superradiant window $0<\omega/(m\Omega_-)<1$, where $\Omega_-=3\pi J/r_0^3$. For the sampled sectors $m=1,2,3$ and spins up to $j=19$, every converged frequency is damped and lies outside this window. Independent integration verifies the low-lying modes, while Kerr spectra provide a separate benchmark for the two-dimensional solver. A limiting radial equation explains why the computed mode frequencies approach the upper edge of the superradiant window with frequency offsets proportional to $(mj)^{-1/2}$ at large $mj$. A complete stability assessment requires further analysis of the unresolved scalar spectrum and of perturbations of the coupled metric-matter system.
item.dc:creator: Mark Sukaiti, Davide Batic, Denys Dutykh

item.title: Thermal Krylov complexity and entropy of inflationary modes with different comoving-wavenumber dependences
item.description: arXiv:2405.01433v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study thermal Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy for primordial scalar modes in three inflationary models with different comoving-wavenumber dependences. These models are canonical single-field inflation, a non-trivial sound speed model, and a modified dispersion relation model. We construct a purified two-mode thermal state and first study its unitary Krylov evolution in an ideal closed system. In the parameter range considered here, the sound-speed correction increases the mean values and oscillation amplitudes of the Krylov quantities. The modified dispersion relation produces a stage-dependent oscillatory structure. We then introduce an independent effective open-system parametrization. The normalized Krylov distribution is controlled by a geometric ratio that combines thermal occupation, coherent spreading, and effective attenuation. We derive explicit expressions for Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy. We also obtain their low- and high-temperature limits. The sound-speed correction enhances the geometric ratio in the adopted parameter range. For the modified dispersion relation, coherent spreading and effective attenuation compete. These results show how thermal occupation and modified mode frequencies control Krylov-space spreading in the three inflationary models.
item.dc:creator: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu

item.title: Scattering and bound observables for spinning particles in Kerr spacetime with generic spin orientations
item.description: arXiv:2405.09687v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive the radial action of a spinning probe particle in Kerr spacetime from the worldline formalism in the first-order form, focusing on linear in spin effects. We then develop a novel covariant Dirac bracket formalism to compute the impulse and the spin kick directly from the radial action, generalizing some conjectural results in the literature and providing ready-to-use expressions for amplitude calculations with generic spin orientations. This allows, for the first time, to find new covariant expressions for scattering observables in the probe limit up to $\mathcal{O}(G^6 s_1 s_2^4)$. Finally, we use the action-angle representation to compute the fundamental frequencies for generic bound orbits, including the intrinsic spin precession, the periastron advance and the precession of the orbital plane.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Gonzo, Canxin Shi

item.title: The Weight of $Spin(32)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ Little Strings: T-duality and Hasse Diagrams
item.description: arXiv:2510.24842v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the worldvolume theories of stacks of $Spin(32)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ heterotic NS5-branes probing a transverse singularity $\mathfrak{g}$. We revisit and extend the original classification by Blum and Intriligator, and show that the resulting 6d Little String Theories (LSTs) are naturally labeled by affine dominant coweights of the singularity $\mathfrak{g}$. This in turn enables us to efficiently arrange these theories into groupings satisfying all known necessary conditions to be T-dual. Using this formulation, we then study the partial order of those coweights, and extend a recently proposed slice-subtraction algorithm to construct Hasse diagrams for LSTs directly from their six-dimensional generalized quivers, allowing us to probe certain properties of their Higgs branch. Along the way, we exploit these techniques to show that the number of duality orbits at maximal flavor rank is determined by the center of the transverse singularity $\mathfrak{g}$, and provide a simplified proof of a monotonicity theorem for this class of theories. Finally, we show how some of our techniques can be extended to other classes of 6d theories, such as Type-II LSTs and SCFTs.
item.dc:creator: Hamza Ahmed, Florent Baume, Paul-Konstantin Oehlmann

item.title: Three-charge black holes from the worldsheet
item.description: arXiv:2511.02499v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the general asymptotically flat, doubly-rotating, three-charge black hole uplifted to a family of NS5-F1-P black brane solutions of Type IIB supergravity. We construct a null-gauged WZW model whose target-space geometry reproduces this background in the NS5 decoupling limit, and show that the gauging parameters precisely satisfy the appropriate consistency conditions on the perturbative string spectrum. Through an analytic continuation and an appropriate limit, this model relates to a recently studied construction describing strings on smooth, horizonless geometries. We further analyze the supersymmetric and extremal three-charge configuration, corresponding to the ten-dimensional uplift of the (NS5-decoupled) BMPV black hole, and show that it requires a novel class of null-gauged WZW models. Our construction provides explicit examples of worldsheet CFTs that capture string dynamics on certain black hole geometries with linear dilaton asymptotics.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Massai, Enrico Turetta

item.title: New Projection Operators for Planar Electrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2512.12873v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we provide a new construction of a set of projection operators and apply it to obtain the propagator of three-dimensional models of electrodynamics; in particular, we consider the Maxwell-Lee-Wick-Chern-Simons, Maxwell-Deser-Jackiw electrodynamics and nonlocal infinite derivative electrodynamics. In order to prove the efficacy of these operators, we perform a causality and unitarity analysis to investigate the presence of ghosts and tachyons.
item.dc:creator: Fl\'avio P. Cruz, Jos\'e A. Santos, Victor J. V. Otoya

item.title: On theta function expressions of cyclic products of fermion correlation functions in genus two
item.description: arXiv:2601.08664v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In arXiv:2211.09069, significant progress was made in decomposing simple products of fermion correlation functions, and in summing over spin structures of superstring amplitudes in genus two under cyclic constraints. In this manuscript we consider part of the same subject using a framework in which one of the branch points of the genus two curve is fixed at infinity. This framework is a direct generalization of the popular one in the case of genus one. We address some of the issues that remained unresolved in our previous paper arXiv:2209.14633. We show that the spin structures of the simple products of fermion correlation functions with cyclic conditions depend only on the Pe-function values at the half-periods of the genus two surface, for any number of factors in the products. Similar to the genus one case, we can provide basis functions to decompose the product. Consequently, the trilinear relations found in arXiv:2211.09069 can be derived from the known set of differential equations of genus two Pe-functions by setting the variables equal to the half-periods of the non-singular and even spin structures, as is the case for genus one. Based on these considerations, we present a procedure for expressing the results of decomposed formulae in terms of the unique genus two theta function for two, three, and four point cases, and discuss a realistic approach for calculating six point function. A general formula for the expression of the results in terms of the theta function for the product of an arbitrary number of the fermion correlation functions is not yet derivable.
item.dc:creator: A. G. Tsuchiya

item.title: Spinning States and Unitarity in 3D Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2604.14492v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit the proposal to cure the negative density of states in the three-dimensional gravitational path integral by adding spinning states whose spin scales with the central charge. We show that sub-extremal and extremal spinning states below the black hole threshold can cancel the known negativities, and interpret these states as bulk spinning defects. Additionally, certain overspinning states above the black hole threshold can cure these negativities while preserving the spectral gap. The overspinning states were previously interpreted as classical spinning strings; we instead identify them as overspinning BTZ geometries, which are smooth pure gravity quotients of AdS$_3$ with no fixed points. All of these spinning geometries exhibit causal pathologies in their Lorentzian continuations. Moreover, the overspinning geometries arise from mixed elliptic-hyperbolic identifications and contain a formally real chiral temperature. We also generalize the computation of scalar correlators to the extremal background and propose a quotient-motivated image expression for the overspinning geometries.
item.dc:creator: Ziyi Li

item.title: On Generalized Statistics and Stability in $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-Graded Supersymmetric Yang-Mills Theory
item.description: arXiv:2604.19415v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the standard formulation of relativistic quantum field theory, a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-graded structure is assumed to realize locality and the boson-fermion dichotomy. While $\mathbb{Z}_2^n$-graded extensions are known to be allowed at the level of symmetry, their realization in interacting quantum field theories remains unclear. In this paper, we construct a classical minimal $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded supersymmetric Yang-Mills theory. We derive the invariant action and show that all kinetic terms have the correct sign, indicating the absence of classical ghost-like instabilities. Moreover, the positivity of the Hamiltonian follows from the $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded supersymmetry algebra. As a result, we show that $\mathbb{Z}_2^2$-graded generalized statistics can be realized at the classical level in a stable interacting supersymmetric gauge theory.
item.dc:creator: Ren Ito, Akio Nago, Shou Tanigawa

item.title: Perturbative Coulomb branches on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$: the global D-term potential
item.description: arXiv:2604.27066v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a Wilsonian description of perturbative D-terms in 4d $\mathcal N=1$ gauge theories on $\mathbb R^3\times S^1$ with chiral Kaluza--Klein spectra. A closed-form, one-loop-exact coefficient of the auxiliary D fields, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos parameters and globally valid throughout the holonomy space, determines the leading holonomy potential away from massless thresholds. We establish uniform weak-coupling control there and match across thresholds by retaining the light fields. Gauge-anomaly cancellation renders the Coulomb-slice vacuum equations affine within each chamber bounded by the thresholds, enabling exact linear analysis of their zero sets and numerical reconstruction through DBSCAN clustering of approximate zeros, LPCA denoising, and RANSAC hyperplane detection. Complementing the rank-one applications of the accompanying Letter, we study flavor-twist dependence in the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ $\mathcal N=4$ theory, and illustrate the numerical reconstruction in higher-rank R-twisted Argyres--Douglas reductions of interest in the SCFT/VOA correspondence. We also relate the same D-term data to leading stationary-phase equations of supersymmetric partition functions and a decompactification limit of the torus twisted superpotential.
item.dc:creator: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Daniel J. Resnick

item.title: Background-independent one-loop renormalization of tensor and scalar primordial spectra
item.description: arXiv:2607.06042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a background-independent renormalization framework for one-loop primordial spectra. We apply it to two observables: the scalar-induced tensor spectrum sourced by a minimally coupled spectator field, and the scalar spectrum generated by potential self-interactions. In both cases, the UV part of the loops is isolated and, using the universal WKB behavior of the internal modes, the UV poles are extracted analytically and absorbed into local counterterms without having to specify either the background evolution or the full dynamics of the field running in the loop. This yields finite model-independent expressions for the renormalized spectra amenable to numerical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Guillermo Ballesteros, Jes\'us Gamb\'in Egea, Flavio Riccardi

item.title: Projections and topological classification of black hole thermodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.07364v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Black hole thermodynamic topology has evolved from classifications based on global topological numbers to more refined schemes including boundary behavior. This development motivates a deeper question: how are different topological manifestations connected within the complete thermodynamic structure? In this paper, we propose the thermodynamic projection conjecture, which seeks to address this question by examining different topological manifestations in the context of the complete thermodynamic structure and exploring their underlying physical connections and formation mechanisms. As a representative application of this idea, we investigate temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions, in which the topological number varies with temperature while the physical parameters are held fixed. We examine how the complete thermodynamic structure gives rise to different topological outcomes on different temperature slices. Our results demonstrate that temperature-dependent thermodynamic topological phase transitions arise from boundary effects, whereas the pairwise generation or annihilation of equilibrium states in the interior leaves the total topological number unchanged. These results establish that, at fixed physical parameters, the topological differences observed on different temperature slices originate from the same complete thermodynamic structure and can be understood within a unified framework of thermodynamic projections. Furthermore, this study offers a new approach to understanding black hole thermodynamic structures and their rich physical behavior through the interplay between global structures and their local manifestations.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu

item.title: Perusing confining pseudoreal theories: hints of emerging massless spin-1 bosons
item.description: arXiv:2607.09531v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solving quantum field theory, which is at the basis of the standard model of particle interactions, is one of the main tasks of contemporary theoretical physics. Minimal asymptotically free pseudoreal theories, containing one or two species of massless Weyl fermions in pseudoreal representations of the gauge group, flow towards a poorly understood infrared dynamics. We provide a comprehensive study of all non-supersymmetric pseudoreal theories, first identifying the ones that likely flow towards a conformal dynamics. Assuming that the remaining ones confine, we find that tumbling hints the possible formation of a non-trivial condensate dynamics, consistently with other symmetry considerations. All but one one-species theories may feature at least one massless spin-1 state. Instead, the only confining two-species theory likely features two massless spin-1 states and one Nambu-Goldstone boson. These expectations must be further tested, for instance by use of Lattice simulations, the functional renormalization group, and supersymmetric analogs.
item.dc:creator: Giacomo Cacciapaglia, Konstantinos Kollias

item.title: Magnetic corrections to the fermionic Casimir effect with Lorentz symmetry violation and a compactified extra dimension
item.description: arXiv:2607.15212v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work I study the effect of a magnetic field on the Casimir effect due to a massive, charged fermion field that violates Lorentz invariance in an aether-like manner while maintaining CPT, in a space with one toroidally compactified extra dimension. I take the fermion field to obey MIT bag boundary conditions on two identical square parallel plates. I do this investigation using the zeta function technique that enables me to calculate the Casimir energy and pressure for a massless fermion, and one with a light mass, in the presence of a constant magnetic field perpendicular to the plates. I examine the cases of timelike Lorentz violation, of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction of the magnetic field, of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction perpendicular to the magnetic field, and of spacelike Lorentz violation in the direction of the compactified extra dimension. In all scenarios, I find simple and accurate analytic expressions of the magnetic field dependent Casimir energy and pressure.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Erdas

item.title: Krylov complexity and spectral density of BMN matrix model
item.description: arXiv:2607.24632v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We use Krylov complexity as a typical diagnostic of quantum many body dynamics in the context of BMN matrix model at large mass gap. We calculate several physical entities, for example, the moments and return amplitudes at large mass deformation. We calculate them for both spread complexity of states as well as Krylov growth of operators in the matrix model. We propose a general expression for the moments at any given order $n$. We also discuss orthogonal polynomials for spread as well as operator Krylov complexity. In the context of the Krylov operator growth we further compute the spectral function and the density of states. A careful analysis of the spectral function near the resonance reveals various IR divergences in addition to the physical collective modes. These collective modes appear to be exceptionally stable due to large mass gap. On the other hand, the UV of the theory appears to be extremely damped due to higher scattering rates. We carefully diagnose these IR divergences near resonance which reveals that these collective modes are in fact non-propagating and should be thought of as diffusion modes or relaxation modes with infinite relaxation time. We also calculate the Krylov variance and Krylov entropy for the matrix model and in particular at early time. The linear early time growth of the Krylov entropy confirms the onset of quantum chaos in the matrix model at large mass gap.
item.dc:creator: Dibakar Roychowdhury

item.title: Gravitational Waves from Multiple Cosmic Superstrings and the Overshoot Problem
item.description: arXiv:2607.26124v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Post inflationary string cosmology can feature an initial population of multiple species of cosmic superstrings whose tension is controlled by a modulus rolling over a steep potential toward a late-time minimum. We perform a full analysis of the associated dynamical system, finding that overshooting the minimum is prevented by the friction of a radiation background of gravitational waves produced from the early decay of effective strings arising from NS5- and D3-branes wrapped around internal cycles. On the other hand, fundamental strings survive longer and decay when the modulus is oscillating around the minimum and they have about $1/3$ of the total energy density. The spectrum of gravitational waves generated by the decays of these multiple cosmic superstrings, even if diluted by a late epoch of modulus domination, can still result in a high-frequency, multi-peaked signal, offering an observational signature of generic features of string theory.
item.dc:creator: Luca Brunelli, Michele Cicoli, Muhammad Hassan, Seyed Ehsan Qoreishi, Francisco Gil Pedro

item.title: Critical and multicritical Kasner scaling in holographic phase transitions
item.description: arXiv:2608.04522v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how holographic phase transitions imprint their scaling laws on the local Kasner geometry inside Einstein-scalar black holes. At fixed double-trace coupling, we derive the near-critical scaling of the deviation of the first-epoch Kasner exponent from the Schwarzschild value: $p_t^{(1)}+\frac{1}{3} \propto O^2 \propto (T_c-T)^{1/r}$, where $O$ denotes the boundary condensate and $r$ labels ordinary criticality ($r=1$), tricriticality ($r=2$), and higher multicriticality ($r\geq3$). A super-exponential scalar potential generates a sequence of Kasner epochs separated by scalar-field bounces. We further find that any later epoch that can be tracked continuously across the transition inherits the same temperature exponent, while its coefficient depends on the epoch. Numerical solutions confirm these predictions for the ordinary and tricritical cases. Finally, we show analytically that the leading irrelevant exponent of the infrared fixed point governs the low-temperature Kasner scaling, and verify the resulting scaling numerically for the first Kasner exponent.
item.dc:creator: Ling-Long Gao, Yan Liu, Hong-Da Lyu

item.title: Cosmological Collider Signals From a Triangle Loop
item.description: arXiv:2609.09288v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Triangular loop signals appear frequently in cosmological collider models but their analytical forms remain unknown due to multiple technical challenges. Here, we determine for the first time the leading analytical cosmological collider signals generated by a massive scalar triangle loop in inflationary bispectrum and trispectrum. Combining a directional cutting rule with partial Mellin-Barnes representations, we obtain both the local and nonlocal trispectrum signals in a soft limit and derive the leading signal in the squeezed bispectrum. Remarkably, all these signals are reproduced by the corresponding bubble diagram with a single effective pinched coupling. Signals beyond leading order and cases with arbitrary internal masses, spins, and interactions can be generated within the same framework. Our approach also provides a systematic route to extracting analytical loop signals from general cosmological correlators.
item.dc:creator: Zhehan Qin, Zhong-Zhi Xianyu

item.title: Metric Source Completions and Integrability in Celestial Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2609.10637v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Opposite-helicity soft limits carry ordering information, whereas a metric generating functional has a symmetric mixed response. We compare these structures for Einstein tree amplitudes, retaining the full momentum-conservation distribution. Normalized transport of primary sources fixes the metric response, and a common Banerjee--Pasterski prescription fixes the two ordered scattering currents on compact regular hard packets. At the reference metric, both ordered scattering responses agree with the transport Hessian, so the two matching defects vanish separately. A four-hard-particle example displays the same nonzero recoil coefficient in both orders and in the transport Hessian; an overlapping-source packet resolves the lower-order spin-frame contact. Six-graviton factorization independently tests the recoil and undifferentiated coefficients of the ordering difference. At seven points, angular integration produces a nonzero relative current whose connector variation contains a conjugate bulk term. We derive this term and its cancellation under coherent transport; global cubic scattering matching still requires the physical Ward comparison on the remaining singular overlaps. Transporting the states, kernels and inverse chains together gives a finite Ward identity and coefficientwise reconstruction for that chosen family. Regular packets leave extensions supported solely on excluded hard--hard coincidences undetermined, and the vacuum functional, independent of the hard sources, remains free.
item.dc:creator: Yingnan Xu, Shuangshuang Chu

item.title: Holography for integrable field theories
item.description: arXiv:2609.34909v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop a holographic dual to the integrable field theories built from $4d$ Chern-Simons theory. The dual theory is a topological string on a generalized Calabi-Yau manifold, which is entirely encoded in a geometric object we call a planar spectral curve. We describe the RG flow for a planar integrable field theory as a geometric flow on the moduli of planar spectral curves. This description is valid at all orders in the 't Hooft coupling. We compute this flow explicitly up to two loops in many examples, and find an exact match with known field theory results. At one loop this includes a wide class of models. At two loops we reproduce the RG flow for the principal chiral model with WZ term, and for a class of integrable $\sigma$-models with target $U(N) \times U(N)$.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Costello, Joaquin Liniado

item.title: Relative entropy of entanglement and tripartite minimal surface
item.description: arXiv:2609.38815v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose a holographic dual of the relative entropy of entanglement for a boundary tripartition $A:B:C$. Our proposal is that, at the leading order, \begin{align} E_R(\rho_{AB}) = \frac{1}{4G_N}\Big[\mathrm{Area}(\Gamma_{\min}) - \mathrm{Area}(\gamma_{AB})\Big] \notag \end{align} where $\Gamma_{\min}$ is the minimal bulk tripartition surface and $\gamma_{AB}$ is the minimal surface homologous to $AB$. For a general random tensor network, we prove the corresponding upper bound by constructing a separable state associated with $\Gamma_{\min}$ and evaluating its relative entropy. We also establish the matching lower bound rigorously for networks of one, two, and three Haar random tensors by bounding the maximal tripartite product-state overlap. In appropriate geometries, the minimal tripartition surface can form a nontrivial tri-junction resembling the Mercedes logo.
item.dc:creator: Takato Mori, Beni Yoshida

item.title: Trinity of Carrollian Gravity: Dynamically Equivalent Formulations of Magnetic Carrollian Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2610.01976v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we extend the paradigm of the Geometrical Trinity of Gravity to the Carrollian geometry to construct a comprehensive framework of dynamically equivalent theories for Magnetic Carrollian gravity. Utilizing the inherent ambiguities and freedoms of affine connections on degenerate metrics, we systematically relax the metric-compatibility and zero-torsion constraints of the rigid magnetic sector. By imposing global flatness on these modified connections, we prove that the curvature of a Magnetic Carrollian universe can be dynamically traded for isolated kinetic energy densities of torsion and non-metricity. Unlike the Lorentzian Trinity which maps gravity to alternative gravitational frameworks, the Carrollian equivalences can also map spacetime geometry to non-gravitational theories. Specifically, we demonstrate that intrinsic torsion recovers Electric Carrollian gravity as the Teleparallel equivalent of Magnetic Carroll gravity; purely spatial torsion reproduces kinetic terms stracturally similar to the magnetic Hamiltonian of scalar-charge Fracton gauge theory; and temporal torsion sectors map independently to $U(1)$ Maxwell electric fields and Carroll-Weyl conformal dilaton theories. Finally, by formulating a Symmetric Teleparallel Carroll connection with minimal non-metricity, we show that the Magnetic Carrollian Lagrangian is dynamically equivalent to an ultralocal, isotropic Electric Carrollian gravity upon exploiting the present freedoms in connection. These results establish a geometric dictionary translating Carrollian gravitational dynamics into the language of tensor gauge theories, electromagnetism, and dilaton theory.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Ahmadi-Jahmani, Aliasghar Parvizi

item.title: Singlet sector of the vector model with angular potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.09815v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the singlet sector of large-$N$, $O(N)$ vector model on $S^1_\beta\times S^2_r$ in presence of an angular potential $\Omega$. We compute the free energy of the model both at the free fixed point as well as the non-trivial fixed point. The model undergoes a phase transition when the temperature $T$ and angular potential attain the relation $T^2r^2\sim N (1-\omega^2)$, where $\omega=r\Omega$ and $r$ is the radius of $S^2$, with $Tr\gg1$, at both the fixed points, with different numerical coefficients. The transition was studied earlier at zero angular potential at $Tr\sim \sqrt{N}$. The holonomy eigenvalue distribution, having support on the full circle below the transition, develops a gap above it, called the Gross-Witten-Wadia transition. The angular potential introduces an additional parameter to such a transition, tuning it, the transition can occur even at a fixed temperature. We show that for the free model transition can occur as $1-\omega^2\sim 1/N$ while $Tr\sim O(1)$. For the interacting model the computation is performed at a limit $Tr\gg1$, thus we show the same at a large but fixed temperature which does not scale as $\sqrt{N}$. In the ungapped phase, the free energy exhibits a double pole near $\omega^2=1$ for both the fixed points. This is possibly due to the fact that the theory projected onto the singlets is non-local and therefore need not obey the leading simple pole scaling of a local thermal effective action.
item.dc:creator: Srijan Kumar

item.title: $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes from the spectral edge of DSSYK and supersymmetric extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.13899v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The $q$-deformed Weil-Petersson volumes of Do and Norbury are the top-degree parts of Okuyama's discrete volumes, which are defined by topological recursion on the spectral curve of the double-scaled SYK (DSSYK) model. We show that the same $q$-deformed volumes can also be obtained from a double-scaled matrix model whose disk density is found by zooming in on the soft edges of the DSSYK density. Applying the same procedure to the hard edge of $\mathcal{N}=1$ DSSYK, we obtain candidate $q$-deformed $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes. They are polynomials of fixed degree, and they reduce to $\mathcal{N}=1$ super Weil-Petersson volumes in a scaled $q\to1$ limit. These candidate volumes differ from the $\mathcal{N}=1$ volumes of Do and Norbury in (arXiv:2510.12431) up to what we call ``irrelevant'' contributions which exactly vanish in the scaled $q\to 1$ limit. Together, these results demonstrate how $q$-deformed volumes can be naturally associated to the spectral edges of various DSSYK models and provides an intuitive way to construct them in supersymmetric contexts.
item.dc:creator: Wasif Ahmed, Joydeep Naskar, Krishan Saraswat

item.title: Modular Flow and Holographic Timelike Entanglement Entropy in AdS and Flat Holography
item.description: arXiv:2610.17165v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Timelike entanglement entropy provides a useful probe of holographic theories, yet an explicit bulk realization of the modular flow underlying its timelike extremal curve construction has so far been lacking. We construct modular flows associated with spacelike and timelike intervals in AdS$_{3}$/CFT$_{2}$ and extend this framework to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$. Beginning with the boundary symmetry generators, we explicitly derive the boundary modular flows and extend them into the bulk, providing a systematic procedure that relates bulk modular flows to the extremal curves and holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. For spacelike intervals, the resulting bulk modular flows determine the extremal curves, whose integrated line elements reproduce the standard holographic entanglement entropy. We then generalize this approach to timelike intervals, explicitly constructing the modular flows whose fixed points reproduce the extremal spacelike and timelike curves, which give the holographic timelike entanglement entropy. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first explicit construction of the modular flow associated with a timelike extremal curve for a timelike interval. The same procedure is then carried over to flat$_{3}$/CCFT$_{2}$, which gives rise to the holographic (timelike) entanglement entropy. Finally, we show that the flat space results obtained in this work can be recovered from their AdS$_3$ counterparts in the flat space limit.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Hakami Shalamzari, Zahra Paygozar, Mahdi Kord Zangeneh

item.title: Holographic Pseudo Entropy from the Rindler Method in AdS and Flat Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.17239v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Via the Rindler method, we study holographic timelike entanglement entropy (TEE) for a general timelike interval in AdS$_3$/CFT$_2$ and flat$_3$/CCFT$_2$. The TEE is the pseudo entropy of a timelike interval. In the bulk, the imaginary part of the TEE comes from a timelike geodesic. After a Rindler transformation to a rotating BTZ black hole, the two spacelike extremal curves lie on the inner and outer horizons, and exchanging $l_u\leftrightarrow \ell l_\phi$ takes one to the other. We clarify the geometric role of the timelike extremal curve in the Rindler frame. We show that it is the line $\tilde U=\tilde V=0$ stretched between the two horizons, starting on the inner horizon, touching the outer horizon at its midpoint, and returning to the inner one. No such curve exists outside the region between the horizons. Its length, $i\pi\ell$, is independent of the interval, and it alone produces the imaginary part $i\pi c/6$. We follow the same procedure in flat space holography, where the spacelike curve sits on the cosmological horizon and the timelike curve lies between the cosmological horizon and timelike infinity. Evaluating the holographic TEE for a timelike interval in CCFT$_2$ on the plane, we find that, in contrast with the cylinder, the real and imaginary parts are equal.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Hakami Shalamzari, Zahra Paygozar, Mahdi Kord Zangeneh

item.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2610.20589v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using a novel multipole re-summation technique, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order, and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. This serves as a non-trivial check on our results. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.
item.dc:creator: R. Loganayagam, Avi Wadhwa

item.title: All Order Gravitational Wave Tails from Classical Soft Theorem for Subleading Post-Newtonian Expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.20770v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The low-frequency gravitational waveform emitted in a classical scattering process contains an infinite tower of late- and early-time tail terms of the form $u^{-r}(\ln|u|)^{r-1}$, $r \geq 1$. In the Newtonian limit, the coefficients of this entire tower have recently been shown to be universal, i.e. fixed by the asymptotic data of the scattering objects alone. At the retained order in the velocity expansion, these leading-logarithmic tails are determined to all orders in Newton's constant $G$. We extend this result to the first subleading order in the post-Newtonian expansion of the asymptotic states. We consider scattering of an arbitrary number of incoming and outgoing nonrelativistic objects interacting only through gravity at long range, and we derive the complete tower of tail terms at this order. The correction arises from the first subleading term in the retardation expansion and is determined by the asymptotic Newtonian trajectories of the massive particles. Its coefficients are again determined entirely by the asymptotic trajectories and are independent of the details of the interaction. For $2\to2$ scattering, the leading-logarithmic series can be summed in closed form. Our results agree with a relativistic conjecture proposed in earlier work arXiv:2610.07134.
item.dc:creator: Debanjan Karan, Babli Khatun

item.title: Boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in holography
item.description: arXiv:2610.26218v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the boundary preparation of strong Mpemba states in a probe Abelian Higgs model on a fixed AdS black brane. Different drives ending at the same charge density can prepare states with different slow mode amplitudes. Two pulses cancel the slowest mode at linear order, but charge exchange during preparation and radial Maxwell feedback regenerate a slow tail at cubic order. We derive the complete cubic response from the lower order field equations, including feedback after source removal, and use it to predict a compensating pulse. Full nonlinear evolution confirms that the compensation reduces the residual slow amplitude from third to fifth order in the source strength. For a representative protocol, the slow amplitude is reduced by a factor of about 600 relative to linear cancellation. This extends the fast relaxation window without changing the final quasinormal mode spectrum. Further nonlinear tuning suppresses the estimated residual amplitude to the level of numerical resolution. The prepared states can overtake a weakly driven reference despite having a larger excess free energy at source removal. Three pulses also suppress a second slow channel over the resolved time window and reveal interference between faster modes. Starting from a common initial state, controls with zero net charge transfer reach a given relaxation threshold sooner than passive relaxation, even when the full control duration is included.
item.dc:creator: Yu Shi, Xinwu Liu, Liping Li, Chikun Ding, Yuebing Zhou, Changqing Liu, Sheng Long

item.title: Mapping AdS$_4$ quantum gravity via the Bethe Ansatz formula
item.description: arXiv:2610.27097v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The topologically twisted index of 3d ADHM theory can be written as a sum over solutions to the Bethe Ansatz Equations (BAEs) of the XXZ-type model constructed from quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$. Via a novel numerical algorithm, we solve for all $p(N)$ physical solutions at $N\leq 21$, where $p(N)$ denotes the number of partitions of $N$. Surveying these solutions, we find that in addition to the known "1-cut" solution dual to dyonic black holes, where the gauge holonomies are distributed along a single curve in the complex plane, there are "dressed" 1-cut solutions dual to combined configurations of the black hole and M2-branes, $m$-cut solutions dual to $\mathbb{Z}_m$ orbifolds of the black hole, a discrete family of solutions interpolating between the 1-cut and 3-cut solutions whose bulk dual is not yet identified, together with other exotic solutions, at each value of $N$. We show that the $1,2,3$-cut solutions and interpolating solutions all have a well-defined large $N$ limit, and analytically compute their leading order distribution of gauge holonomies. Whenever possible, we fit the contributions of the solutions to the index to all orders in the $1/N$ expansion with high-precision numerics, and extract the leading non-perturbative correction. With exceptions, these are matched with the results of equivariant localization in the bulk, and the action of wrapped M2-branes respectively.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Peng, Xuao Zhang, Ziruo Zhang

item.title: Beyond the Fock Vacuum in Finite-$N$ Bilocal Algebras of Vector Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.30572v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We discuss the finite-$N$ Hilbert space of bilocal operators that underlies bilocal holography of vector models, beyond the sector built on the Fock vacuum. If the microscopic oscillator Fock space carries a multiplicity-free dual action of a compact color group $G$ and a bilocal algebra, Howe duality implies that projection to the derived subgroup $[G,G]$ selects precisely the characters of the abelianization $G^{\rm ab}=G/[G,G]$ that occur in the Fock space. Thus $O(N)/SO(N)=\mathbb Z_2$ gives two sectors, $U(N)/SU(N)=U(1)$ gives integer determinant-charge sectors, while $Sp(N)$ is perfect and gives no additional sector; Bose/Fermi statistics and the number of modes determine which sectors are actually realized. We construct the epsilon and determinant backgrounds that generate these sectors, together with their finite-$N$ constraints and Casimirs, and find that the two bosonic $O(N)$ sectors are not distinguished by any Casimir. Using group-integral projectors, we derive explicit sector-resolved characters for the $O(N)$ and $U(N)$ theories. Around each new background we solve the constraints with auxiliary oscillators, which form a Fermi sea for bosonic matter. In the free vector model on $\mathbb R\times S^2$ the lowest states in the new sectors are baryonic primaries; we determine their energies, degeneracies and spin content exactly at finite $N$, together with their lowest energy at fixed angular momentum.
item.dc:creator: Byoungjoon Ahn, Robert de Mello Koch, Vatsal Garg, Antal Jevicki, Junggi Yoon

item.title: Exact holographic superfluid at the Bogomolny point: transport, large charge, and R\'enyi entropies
item.description: arXiv:2610.40371v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The probe-limit Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ is a standard holographic model of a strongly coupled superfluid, usually solved numerically. With the scalar mass at the Breitenlohner-Freedman bound and the quartic coupling at the Bogomolny value, its condensed phase has a closed form on every static, uncharged AdS$_5$ background with maximally symmetric spatial sections. We prove that it is the global minimum of the free energy at fixed charge, and linearly stable, as is any nodeless condensate of the model in standard quantization with nonnegative quartic coupling and no superflow. On the planar black brane it is the superfluid at all temperatures below $T_c$: the superfluid fraction follows the Gorter-Casimir two-fluid law exactly, and the speed and attenuation of sound are in closed form. In global AdS$_5$ it is the lowest state of charge $Q$ on $\mathbb{R}\times S^3$ within the model, with its scaling dimension in closed form at all $Q$, classically in the bulk. Its excitations include towers, from an infrared fixed point of the probe sector, that the superfluid effective theory does not describe. On the hyperbolic black holes that compute charged R\'enyi entropies of a ball, it is a homogeneous hairy phase whose condensate does not fall off toward the entangling surface. With a pinning field there, the phase sets in at R\'enyi index exactly one at zero chemical potential, as found for a neutral scalar. Well below a bound on the quartic coupling, the static, homogeneous solutions computed at other couplings and masses keep an infrared fixed point with towers, but not the exact two-fluid law.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu

item.title: The running of Weyl gauged gravity: asymptotic freedom, its obstruction, and a way out
item.description: arXiv:2610.40769v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the one-loop beta functions of quadratic gravity in Weyl conformal geometry, the gauge theory of diffeomorphisms and dilatations with a dynamical Weyl gauge boson. The divergences are extracted diagrammatically in the background field method, with a gauge fixing procedure adapted to the semidirect product structure of the gauge group. The Weyl-tensor coupling and the Weyl gauge coupling are asymptotically free, and the running of the latter is special, being independent of the other couplings and of any two-derivative matter content. The obstruction to an ultraviolet completion comes from the square of a Weyl-covariant curvature scalar, denoted $\widehat{R}{}^2$: the flow of the corresponding coupling has no fixed point in the physically interesting region and becomes trivial, the only real fixed points require a decoupled Weyl boson and a tachyonic scalar mode. This also holds when including the Standard Model with any nonminimal Higgs coupling and, more generally, for any matter with two-derivative kinetic terms. Weyl-invariant four-derivative scalars with a sufficiently large coupling to $\widehat{R}{}^2$ can remove the obstruction, producing a fixed point in the physical region that is ultraviolet attractive in all directions and has a nonvanishing Weyl gauge coupling.
item.dc:creator: Diego Buccio, Fabrizio Chicconi, Luca Parente, Omar Zanusso

item.title: A Common Type II Origin of Galilean and Carroll Superstrings
item.description: arXiv:2610.41582v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the relativistic Type-II superalgebras, once the fundamental-string winding charge is retained alongside the momentum, admit a single non-Lorentzian contraction with two invariant translation ideals, whose complementary quotients yield Galilean and magnetic-Carroll superalgebras. The complementary vector charge required for this structure is thus intrinsic to string theory. The IIA realization is particle-like and the IIB realization string-like, a distinction fixed by chirality, and spacelike T-duality relates the two while preserving each non-Lorentzian structure. The same contraction is finite on the doubled Green--Schwarz action, including all fermion terms and local kappa symmetry, where the two supersymmetries appear as the two polarizations of a single worldsheet theory. These results unify two distinct non-Lorentzian corners of string theory within a common Type-II origin and open a route toward a broader web of non-Lorentzian dualities and possible holographic generalizations.
item.dc:creator: Mehmet Ozkan, Utku Zorba

item.title: Transgression branes in seven dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A seven dimensional theory with branes, described by a Transgression Action is investigated. The theory has special properties owing to the factorization of the trace used to define the Transgression form. It is shown that in some cases the theory is similar to the models of branes proposed by Nepomechie, Wu and Zee as a higher dimensional generalization of models of particles with fractional statistics of Wilczek, Wu and Zee. Static Euclidean solutions are presented, and compared with similar solutions of Nepomechie,Wu and Zee. Then Lorentzian static solutions are considered, based in solutions of constant curvature black holes presented by Ba\~nados and further studied by Guilleminot, Olea and Petrov. Topological phases and their implications for quantum statistics are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Mora (CURE, Universidad de la Rep\'ublica, Uruguay)

item.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic R\'enyi defects
item.description: arXiv:2611.03413v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The R\'enyi entropies of a ball are computed by the R\'enyi defect (the twist operator viewed as a conformal defect), which in holography is dual to a hyperbolic black hole. We identify hyperbolic black holes with homogeneous charged scalar hair as conformal defects that break the U(1) symmetry. At large $N$ and for repulsive self-interactions, conformality loss of the R\'enyi defect turns explicit symmetry breaking into spontaneous breaking: below a critical index $n_*$ the symmetry-breaking defect is reached only with an explicit source on the entangling surface; at $n_*$ the dimension of a defect operator from a light charged scalar turns complex; beyond $n_*$ the R\'enyi defect flows to the symmetry-breaking defect with no source. The condensate, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, instead preserves them outside a layer at the entangling surface, whose width diverges at $n_*$ with Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless scaling. The universal term of the R\'enyi entropy therefore jumps at $n_*$ to that of the symmetry-breaking defect. We demonstrate this mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, with closed-form saddles and defect data, and numerical flows. For a ball we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the radius is large enough, and that it ends at the symmetry-breaking defect as the radius grows.
item.dc:creator: Siqing Yu

item.title: Explicit Symmetry Breaking in Non-Abelian Scalar Theories and One-Loop Renormalization
item.description: arXiv:2611.08493v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the one-loop renormalization of a Yang--Mills--Faddeev--Popov theory deformed by a complex scalar doublet with explicitly broken $SU(2)$ gauge symmetry. At the classical level, we map the complex doublet into a real $SO(4)$ multiplet and discuss its generalization to $SU(N)$ through $SO(2N)$. The symmetry breaking is introduced by splitting the scalar masses and quartic couplings. Using the background field method and the Schwinger--DeWitt technique, we compute the one-loop divergences and establish renormalizability at this order. We derive the beta functions, recovering the known gauge-invariant limit, and analyze the RG flow. Although the Yang--Mills coupling remains asymptotically free, the rescaled quartic couplings have no real fixed points, and the one-loop flow develops a divergence at a finite energy scale, even in the symmetric limit. The asymmetry between the rescaled scalar self-couplings increases toward the UV and decreases toward the IR, within the region of nonnegative scalar self-couplings.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ducastelo de C. C. Lima

item.title: Effect of ultralight dark matter on compact binary mergers
item.description: arXiv:2503.19660v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The growing catalogue of gravitational wave events enables a statistical analysis of compact binary mergers, typically quantified by the binary merger rate density. This quantity can be influenced by ambient factors, following which, in this work we have investigated the impact of dark matter environment on the merger statistics.
