We construct a baseline astrophysical model of eccentric and quasi-circular compact binary mergers and extend it by incorporating a model of ultra light dark matter, which affects the orbital evolution of binaries through accretion and dynamical friction. Our analysis of the merged population of binary progenitors demonstrates that, compared to the baseline model, ULDM can potentially alter the merger statistics for ambient non-zero densities, with the best agreement with GWTC-3 obtained for $\rho_0\sim10^6$ GeV/cm$^3$ and eccentricity $\sim0.5$. A comparison with the gravitational wave data from the GWTC-3 catalogue provides crucial insight into potential observational signatures of the ULDM in merger events, leading to possible constraints on the existence and density of dark matter distribution in galaxies.
item.dc:creator: Kabir Chakravarti, Soham Acharya, Sumanta Chakraborty, Sudipta Sarkar

item.title: On the consistency of non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m black hole solution
item.description: arXiv:2507.16780v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit the non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m black hole solution obtained by smearing the point sources with a Gaussian distribution. We show that while the form of the metric function and the physical properties derived from that remain valid, not all the components of Einstein equations are satisfied: the angular components fail by exactly the Lorentz force density exerted by the electric field on the smeared charge, which the standard electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor leaves unbalanced. We construct an improved energy-momentum tensor that consistently satisfies Einstein equations. It is the unique conserved completion: the standard Maxwell tensor supplemented by an interaction stress supported on the smeared source. The improved tensor leads to a different prediction for the region where the strong energy condition is violated. For certain choice of parameters, our proposal predicts the violation of the energy condition outside the Cauchy horizon, which might be relevant for the stability of the inner horizon and strong cosmic censorship.
item.dc:creator: Gokhan Alkac, Murat Mesta, Gonul Unal

item.title: Discrete gravitational diagram technique and corrections to the Newtonian potential
item.description: arXiv:2601.03228v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: To develop a gravitational diagram technique that is ultraviolet finite, we start from Regge's simplicial gravity and use a bell-shaped form of the measure obtained via functional integration over connection. A "hypercubic" structure is considered (some variables are frozen), it is described by the metric $g_{\lambda \mu}$ at the sites. The measure is known in closed form if the timelike length scale is fixed at a low level. This is possible in the synchronous gauge (properly softened to remove nonphysical infrared singularities). This gauge also allows, with a refined finite-difference form of the action, to match the analytical properties of the propagator to the continuum case. The metric is parameterized to make the measure Lebesgue. The linear part of this parametrization leads to a discrete form of standard Feynman diagrams that approximates finite continuum diagrams and is finite for infinite ones; the nonlinear part gives new vertices and diagrams. The maximum of the measure is at the edge length scale $b = b_{\rm s} \sim \eta^{1/2}$, where $\eta$ defines the free factor like $(- \det \|g_{\lambda \mu}\|)^{\eta/2}$ in the measure and should be a large parameter to ensure true action upon integration over connection. For general perturbative expansion (including both that for the measure and the S matrix) to be free of increasing powers of $\eta$, its initial point must be at $b$ sufficiently close to $b_{\rm s}$; this appears to be a dynamic mechanism for establishing $b$ as an optimal initial point of the perturbative expansion. This technique is applied to Newton's potential. Some of new diagrams, including potentially large ones, are mutually cancelled. The S matrix expansion is analyzed to consist of standard diagrams. These diagrams form series with a small parameter $\eta^{-1}$; one-loop diagrams calculated in the literature represent the leading order.
item.dc:creator: V. M. Khatsymovsky

item.title: Resummed energy loss in extreme-mass-ratio scattering using critical orbits
item.description: arXiv:2602.10089v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Motivated by recent efforts to bridge between weak-field and strong-field descriptions of black-hole binary dynamics, we develop a resummation scheme for post-Minkowskian radiative observables in extreme-mass-ratio scattering, augmented with post-Newtonian terms. Specifically, we derive universal interpolation formulas for the total energy emitted in gravitational waves out to infinity and down the event horizon of the large black hole, valid to leading order in the small mass ratio. We test our formulas using numerical results from direct calculations in black hole perturbation theory. The central idea of our approach is to utilize as a strong-field diagnostic the known form of divergence in the radiated energy along geodesics near the parameter-space separatrix between scattering and plunge. The dominant, logarithmic term of this divergence can be expressed in terms of instantaneous energy fluxes calculated along the unstable circular geodesics that form the separatrix, fluxes that we obtain using interpolation of highly accurate numerical data. The same idea could be applied to bound-orbit radiative observables via either unbound-to-bound mapping or a direct resummation of bound-orbit post-Newtonian expressions.
item.dc:creator: Leor Barack, Riccardo Gonzo, Benjamin Leather, Oliver Long, Niels Warburton

item.title: A new product formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with applications to asymptotics
item.description: arXiv:2602.11329v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We express the $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(z;q)_\infty$ as an infinite product of gamma functions, analogously to how Narukawa expressed the elliptic gamma function as an infinite product of hyperbolic gamma functions. This identity is used to obtain asymptotic expansions when $q$ tends to $1$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Arabi Ardehali, A., Rosengren, H. A New Product Formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with Applications to Asymptotics. Constr Approx (2026)
item.dc:creator: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Hjalmar Rosengren

item.title: Hall Viscosity in the Quark-Gluon Plasma
item.description: arXiv:2603.23498v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the Hall viscosity of the quark gluon plasma (QGP) created in non-central heavy-ion collisions. In the presence of a strong magnetic field or vorticity, rotational symmetry is broken from $O(3)$ to $O(2)$, allowing for two independent Hall viscosities associated with shear deformations transverse and parallel to the symmetry-breaking direction. We find the corresponding constitutive relations by extending the kinetic-theory mechanism to three spatial dimensions and provide parametric estimates of the Hall viscosities under realistic QGP conditions. Both kinetic-theory and holographic estimates indicate that Hall viscosities are comparable in magnitude to the shear viscosity at zero magnetic field. We further show that Hall viscous stresses at hydrodynamic initialization can be as large as standard viscous corrections and identify observable consequences in flow and event-plane correlations.
item.dc:creator: Sukrut Mondkar, Giorgio Torrieri, Matthias Kaminski, Ren\'e Meyer

item.title: Axion Quality in Warped Extra-Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2604.08700v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the axion quality problem in warped extra-dimensional models in which the QCD axion arises as the Wilson-line mode of a five-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge field compactified on an $S^1/\mathbb{Z}_2$ orbifold. Higher-dimensional gauge invariance severely constrains possible sources of Peccei--Quinn symmetry breaking, implying that non-QCD contributions to the axion potential are predominantly generated by nonlocal effects mediated by $U(1)$-charged fields propagating along the compact dimension. We systematically compute these contributions and examine how both the warped geometry and the orbifold fixed points (branes) affect the resulting axion quality. Finally, we classify the parametric suppression of the induced axion potential, thereby identifying the conditions under which warped extra-dimensional axions can achieve sufficiently high quality.
item.dc:creator: Kiwoon Choi, Chang Hyeon Lee, Chang Sub Shin

item.title: Quantum Charge-4e Superconductivity and Possible Deconfined Pseudocriticality in the Attractive SU(4) Hubbard Model
item.description: arXiv:2604.14289v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Unlike conventional charge-2e superconductors, a charge-4e superconductor exhibits long-range coherence of electron quartets rather than Cooper pairs. Clear zero-temperature realizations of charge-4e superconductivity remain rare. Here, we investigate the zero-temperature phase diagram of the attractive SU(4) Hubbard model with numerically exact, large-scale quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) simulations overcoming major technical hurdles. We identify both charge-2e and charge-4e superconducting phases. Upon increasing interaction, charge-2e long-range order vanishes, while charge-4e correlations remain robust and converge with system size, establishing a quartet-condensed phase. Interestingly, across the charge-2e--charge-4e transition, single electrons remain gapped, while charge-2e correlations exhibit an effective anomalous dimension substantially exceeding the conventional O(6) Landau theory prediction. These features motivate a fractionalized framework in which the physical charge-2e order parameter is a composite field coupled to an emergent non-Abelian gauge structure. We formulate an Sp(4) gauge-Higgs theory associating the charge-2e and charge-4e states with Higgs and confined phases, respectively. A one-loop analysis of an SU($N_f$) generalization exhibits a fixed-point collision, motivating deconfined pseudocriticality as a possible interpretation of the observed scaling. Our results establish charge-4e superconductivity as a bona fide zero-temperature phase, provide a simple model for future studies in a numerically exact framework, and suggest an unconventional route to superconducting criticality.
item.dc:creator: Zhou-Quan Wan, Huan Jiang, Xuan Zou, Shiwei Zhang, Shao-Kai Jian

item.title: Inaccessibility of the Schwarzschild Singularity to Quantum Probes
item.description: arXiv:2605.13508v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We revisit the Schwarzschild singularity in a semiclassical setting where the background geometry is classical and quantum effects enter through Bohmian (quantal) trajectories associated with a Klein-Gordon wave function. Using the Madelung-Bohm decomposition of the Klein-Gordon wavefunction, we show that the quantum-modified motion is equivalent to geodesic motion in an effective metric conformally related to Schwarzschild, with a conformal factor fixed by the wavefunction amplitude. Solving the wavefunction equation near $r\to 0$ determines this factor and yields finite curvature invariants, in suitable coordinates the interior extends smoothly and the effective spacetime is geodesically complete. Our result suggests that quantum probes on a prescribed classical background can experience an operationally regular effective geometry, even though the underlying Schwarzschild spacetime itself remains classically singular.
item.dc:creator: Vishnulal Cheriyodathillathu, Tanmay Patil, Saurya Das, Soumen Basak

item.title: Exploring the near-kernel sector of quantum reduced loop gravity
item.description: arXiv:2605.18625v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the near-kernel sector of the Hamiltonian constraint operator in the one-vertex model of quantum reduced loop gravity using exact diagonalisation methods and variational Monte Carlo methods with neural quantum states. The analysis is based on the symmetric Hamiltonian containing both Euclidean and Lorentzian contributions, and on the variational minimization of the positive quadratic operator $\hat{Q}=\hat{C}^2$, where $\hat{C}$ is the symmetric Hamilton constraint, in truncated Hilbert spaces with spin cutoff up to $j_\text{max}=1001$. In the cases where exact diagonalization is possible, the eigenspace of lowest eigenvalue is one- or two-dimensional, and the eigenvalue, as well as the structure of the eigenstates depends on the cutoff. These ground states are entangled across the three edges. The variational method does not find the lowest eigenspace, but near kernel states, i.e., states with components in a number of low lying eigenspaces. For low cutoffs, they also do not factorize across the three edge degrees of freedom. At larger cutoffs, it increasingly finds near kernel states that factorize over the edges, matched with near-unit fidelity by reduced Thiemann coherent states. We discuss some indication that these states are the optimal near-kernel states if factorization is assumed.
item.dc:creator: Ilkka M\"akinen, Hanno Sahlmann, Waleed Sherif

item.title: Collective excitations in quantum gravity condensates
item.description: arXiv:2605.18977v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A central open problem in quantum gravity is to understand how continuum spacetime emerges from quantum-geometric degrees of freedom in a background-independent setting. A many-body perspective suggests that spacetime emerges as a hydrodynamic phase of many atoms of quantum geometry. This idea underlies several approaches to quantum gravity, and it has been explicitly realised in the group field theory formalism. However, quantum fluctuations beyond the mean-field regime remain largely unexplored. We fill this gap by importing Bogolyubov theory to quantum gravity condensates, showing that leading beyond-mean-field effects manifest as collective excitations, in direct analogy with phonons in laboratory Bose-Einstein condensates. We implement the construction in a tractable group field theory model, where condensates of quantum-geometric atoms reproduce nonsingular expanding cosmologies, and derive the leading beyond-mean-field corrections to the emergent Friedmann dynamics. These results identify a new class of quantum-gravity excitations and establish a controlled bridge between microscopic quantum-gravitational dynamics, many-body collective phenomena, and signatures of spacetime emergence.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Calcinari, Adri\`a Delhom, Daniele Oriti

item.title: Electromagnetic duality degeneracy in dynamical black hole mergers
item.description: arXiv:2605.20493v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Electromagnetic duality is a symmetry of the source-free Einstein-Maxwell equations that rotates electric and magnetic fields while leaving the stress-energy tensor invariant. We present the first fully nonlinear realization of this symmetry in dynamical strong-gravity regimes by performing numerical relativity simulations of charged black hole mergers across a continuous duality family. Starting from electrically charged binaries, we generate dyonic and magnetically charged configurations via duality rotations and evolve them within a common numerical framework. We find that all dual configurations exhibit identical spacetime dynamics, while the emitted electromagnetic radiation is related by a rotation of its polarization equal to the duality angle. Our results demonstrate a degeneracy of gravitational observables under electromagnetic duality and provide a concrete mapping between dual configurations at the level of radiation, establishing electromagnetic duality as an organizing principle for dynamical Einstein-Maxwell solutions.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Ferreira, Gabriele Bozzola, Carlos A. R. Herdeiro, Vasileios Paschalidis, Miguel Zilh\~ao

item.title: Revisiting the Axial Anomaly and Chiral Magnetic Effect in Dense Matter, with Applications to Axion Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2606.11713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We explicitly compute the axial anomaly in dense matter and show that it takes the same form as in vacuum, even in the massless limit. This result follows from a subtle cancellation in the anomalous Ward identity between the medium-induced contributions to the divergence of the axial current and to the pseudoscalar density. We then revisit the chiral magnetic effect in a fermionic medium coupled to an axial chemical potential in an external magnetic field. We show that, in the clean limit, the medium supports a persistent, conserved anomalous current carried by fermions. The current is determined by the axial chemical potential and suppressed by the Fermi velocity, in agreement with anomalous axial-current correlation functions. Finally, we discuss applications to axion physics, where axion dark matter acts as an effective axial chemical potential, and estimate how helicity relaxation by impurity scattering limits the induced current in realistic conductors.
item.dc:creator: Deog Ki Hong

item.title: Energy Extraction via Magnetic Reconnection from a Rotating Dyonic Black Hole in $N = 2, \ U(1)^2$ Gauged Supergravity
item.description: arXiv:2606.23862v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study energy extraction via magnetic reconnection from a rotating dyonic black hole in four-dimensional $N=2$, $U(1)^2$ gauged supergravity. Using the Comisso-Asenjo mechanism in the ZAMO frame, we derive the asymptotic hydrodynamic energy per unit enthalpy $\epsilon^{\infty}_\pm$ and determine when reconnection outflows attained negative energy at infinity. By varying the spin $a$, electric and magnetic charges, NUT parameter $N_g$, and gauge coupling $g$, we compute the cutoff magnetization $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and map the region of parameter space that admits $\epsilon^{\infty}_-<0$. We find that $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and the very existence of Comisso-Asenjo extraction are tightly controlled by $g$ and the dyonic charges: increasing $g$ or pushing the charges toward extremality raises $\sigma_0^{\rm cutoff}$ and shrinks the CA-active part of the ergoregion. Unlike Kerr, the spin enters through the normalization factor $\Xi$, and the quartic horizon function $\Delta_g$, so geometric effects from the AdS/NUT deformation dominate the usual frame-dragging enhancement. As a result, the extracted power and efficiency are non-monotonic in $a$ and peak at intermediate spin ($a\sim0.8$); near-extremal rotation is not required for high efficiency, provided $g$ is small and $Q$ is moderate. Efficient extraction further demands extreme magnetization and nearly radial outflows, confining the active reconnection layer to a thin shell, just outside the horizon.
item.dc:creator: Raid M Suleiman, Shanshan Rodriguez, Dominic O. Chang, Leo Rodriguez

item.title: Fermion mass relations in one-parameter modular models
item.description: arXiv:2606.25027v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Modular flavour symmetries provide a possible organizing principle for the Standard Model Yukawa sector, by replacing generic couplings with a potentially small number of modular forms controlled by a single complex modulus. We study the extreme limit of this idea: One-Parameter Models, in which each charged-fermion mass matrix is fixed by a single modular invariant contraction. We develop a systematic method to construct such models, showing that the One-Parameter Model requirement is already highly constraining at the level of possible fermion hierarchies. In a concrete realization, the charged-lepton and down-quark sectors are controlled by the common modulus, leading to exact mass relations at the flavour scale, $m_s^5 = 2\sqrt{2}\,m_d^3m_b^2, \qquad m_\mu^3 = \sqrt{2}\,m_e m_\tau^2, \qquad m_s^2m_\tau = \sqrt{2}\,m_e m_b^2$. We show that, once renormalization-group evolution and selective supersymmetric threshold effects are included, these high-scale relations can be made compatible with low-energy charged-fermion data. Our results provide a working proof of principle for One-Parameter Models and point towards a possible route to the flavour puzzle through highly constrained constructions.
item.dc:creator: Salvador Centelles Chuli\'a, Xueqi Li, Xiang-Gan Liu, Omar Medina, J. T. Penedo

item.title: Exclusive Quark and Gluon Dijet Production as Probes of GPDs at Collider Energies
item.description: arXiv:2607.04482v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study exclusive electroproduction of dijets in the collinear factorization framework as a probe of generalized parton distributions (GPDs). For quark dijet production, we extend previous analyses by including contributions from helicity GPDs and by assessing an additional leading-order electromagnetic channel governed by elastic nucleon form factors. Furthermore, we investigate exclusive gluon dijet production. We compare our prediction to HERA data and provide projections for measurements at the future Electron-Ion Collider.
item.dc:creator: Zhuoyi Pang, Pawe{\l} Sznajder, Lech Szymanowski, Jakub Wagner

item.title: ACT-DR6 consistent inflation in generalised entropic cosmology and $f(Q)$ gravity
item.description: arXiv:2607.06582v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Within the framework of generalised entropic cosmology and its equivalent $f(Q)$ gravity, we construct inflationary scenarios consistent with recent Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT) observations combined with Planck-BAO data. We work with $f(Q)$ gravity and use the reconstruction scheme from which one can obtain an arbitrary cosmological evolution consistent with desirable theoretical or observational considerations. Explicit inflationary cosmologies of the above theory, which pass ACT-Data Release 6 (DR6) data combined with Planck and BAO, are obtained. For $f(Q)$ gravity coupled with scalar, we obtain ACT inflation for large classes of $f(Q)$ via the choice of the scalar potentials. The entropic cosmology based on generalised entropy, which includes most of the known entropies like Tsallis, R\'{e}nyi, Barrow, etc as a particular case, is investigated. The corresponding FRW equations, depending on the parameters of generalised entropy, are presented. Using the correspondence between the generalised entropy and $f(Q)$ gravity, we obtain generalised entropic inflation, which is consistent with the ACT-DR6. At the next step, the entropic gravity coupled with scalar is considered. It is demonstrated how one can obtain ACT-DR6-consistent inflation for such a theory based on any generalised entropy considered in this paper via the choice of scalar potentials. These findings may point towards the correct unifying entropy of the early universe.
item.dc:creator: Shin'ichi Nojiri, Sergei D. Odintsov

item.title: Phonon Angular Momentum Pumping in Curved Membranes
item.description: arXiv:2607.14868v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Flexural vibrations dominate the low-energy spectrum of a flat crystalline membrane but do not couple to phonon Hall viscosity. We show that static curvature couples normal motion to in-plane strain, allowing an oscillatory flexural drive to generate elliptical in-plane motion and pump phonon angular momentum along the surface normal. A net angular momentum persists in randomly rippled membranes, with its magnitude and handedness controlled by the drive and ripple spectra. Transfer of the pumped angular momentum to the support produces a steady torque that reverses with the magnetic field and scales with the mean-square curvature. Using the measured bulk Hall viscosity of $\alpha$-RuCl$_3$ to set the scale, we estimate a torque of order $10^{-23}$--$10^{-22}\,\mathrm{N\,m}$ for a few-layer membrane, within reach of demonstrated torsional sensors. The same flexural-to-shear response provides a probe of phonon Hall viscosity in atomically thin crystals.
item.dc:creator: Pablo A. Morales

item.title: Landau Levels on the Surface of a Cube
item.description: arXiv:2607.25684v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the quantum mechanics of a charged particle confined to the surface of a cube enclosing a magnetic monopole. The magnetic field is chosen to have a constant magnitude on each face and to point along the outward normal, preserving the rotational symmetry of the cube. We formulate the continuum problem using two gauge patches on the cube surface and show that consistency of the wavefunction gives the Dirac quantization condition. Since an explicit vector potential does not remain invariant under ordinary rotations, we construct gauge-modified rotation operators and use them to classify the eigenstates. Even monopole charges are described by the irreducible representations of the cubic rotation group O, while odd monopole charges require the spinorial representations of the binary octahedral group 2O. We compute the spectrum with a gauge-covariant finite-difference discretization and find Landau-level-like manifolds whose degeneracies are split by the discrete cubic symmetry. We also study the corresponding tight-binding Hofstadter problem on the discretized cube. The resulting spectrum contains the usual magnetic subband structure together with additional gap states localized near the cube corners.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Kura, Almila, Bayram Tekin, and Mehmet \"Ozg\"ur Oktel. "Landau levels on the surface of a cube." APS Open Science 1 (2026): 000198

item.title: How does geometry shape quantum emission in rotating bumblebee gravity?
item.description: arXiv:2608.01398v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We compare propagation and static emission estimates in a rotating metric geometry and a stationary metric-affine bumblebee geometry. Their distinct constructions and spatial asymptotics are kept, and normalized Killing times define the physical frequencies and angular velocities. Direct invariant calculations identify the metric-affine outer root and open exterior axes as curvature singularities for generic rotation. The obstruction at bifurcation surface poles concerns the smoothness of the bumblebee field independently. Its mixed meridional component couples angular channels; finite transverse energy fixes the adopted axial condition and defines a self adjoint stationary operator on bounded exterior annuli. For the metric geometry, we construct normalized radiative scalar modes with specified Unruh data, evaluate the horizon frequency transformation, and include spontaneous superradiant emission through the radial scattering map. We prove positivity of the axisymmetric potential and compute numerical transmission factors and a partial scalar energy spectrum alongside an analytical lower bound. The static emission estimates use the stated Stefan-Boltzmann model.
item.dc:creator: A. A. Ara\'{u}jo Filho

item.title: A No-Go Theorem for Order-Two Clifford Electric-Magnetic Duality
item.description: arXiv:2610.02097v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Electromagnetic duality in the toric code has order two at the level of anyon types and acts as a Hadamard-type logical transformation on the encoded quantum information. Here, we ask whether it can likewise be realized microscopically as an order-two Clifford operation. For the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ toric code, we prove that any locality-preserving Clifford realization of electric-magnetic exchange cannot have order two. Our proof is fully general and requires neither translation symmetry with restricted families of system sizes nor a fixed pairing between vertex and plaquette stabilizers. Geometrically, the proof locally emulates the unavoidable crossing between electric and magnetic strings, similar to a cross-cap in a non-orientable manifold. Extending the problem to the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ toric code, we find that an order-two Clifford realization exists for odd $N$, whereas it is impossible for even $N$. Our result shows that the order-two exchange of closed-string operators cannot be extended to an order-two exchange of open-string operators.
item.dc:creator: Shunta Takahashi, Zhi Li, Beni Yoshida

item.title: No Einstein Relation, No Problem: How Relativistic Weakly Coupled Heavy Quarks Equilibrate Beyond Leading Logarithm Anyway
item.description: arXiv:2610.03863v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Relativistic heavy quarks equilibrate even when their microscopic drag and momentum diffusion violate the Einstein relation. We investigate how equilibration proceeds as a function of the coupling and compared to simplified Fokker-Planck models. To do this, we present a detailed calculation of the momentum-transfer kernel in weakly coupled non-Abelian plasmas through strict $\mathcal{O}(g^4)$, and study the resulting dynamics at leading order in the inverse heavy-quark mass. Beyond leading logarithm, its non-Gaussian structure plays a crucial role in equilibration. We examine closely the analytic structure of the evolution kernel, determine the large-order asymptotics of the momentum-transfer cumulants, and show how the kernel's bounded analytic domain fixes asymmetric exponential tails at the level of the momentum transfer probability. Strongly coupled $\mathcal{N}=4$ SYM also features an approximately Gaussian core and exponential tails, but differs in the nature of the kernel's singularities and the velocity dependence of the transport coefficients and tail exponents. These differences have distinct dynamical consequences: for the parameters studied, the persistence of the relativistic population in steeply falling spectra is largely explained by drag alone at very weak coupling, whereas fluctuation-induced survivor bias produces a large relative enhancement at strong coupling. Nevertheless, the shared qualitative structure between weak and strong coupling points the way towards a practical phenomenological description of heavy quarks anchored in first-principles field theory.
item.dc:creator: Jean F. Du Plessis, Bruno Scheihing-Hitschfeld

item.title: Self-Interacting Dark Matter: From Particle Physics Theories to Structure Formation Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.16968v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish a unified theory-to-simulation framework for self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) that integrates three components: (i) a comprehensive, self-contained treatment of its particle-physics foundations and a broad range of model classes; (ii) a systematic, quantitative mapping from microscopic dark-sector physics to structure-formation simulation inputs through explicit expressions and numerical prescriptions; and (iii) the development, implementation, and validation of a broad suite of SIDM algorithms and a dedicated DM decay module in the moving-mesh code AREPO-2. Under (i), we detail the particle content, symmetries, interactions, production mechanisms, and constraints of a broad landscape of elementary and composite SIDM models, and present representative viable benchmark models. Under (ii), the mapping specifies cosmological initial conditions, internal-state masses and populations, reaction networks, velocity- and angle-dependent cross sections, dissipative energy loss, and decay rates and recoil kinematics. We then apply this mapping to a broad range of SIDM model classes. Under (iii), we implement and validate SIDM algorithms with constant and velocity-dependent cross sections, covering isotropic and anisotropic scattering, multi-state elastic and inelastic reactions, and dissipative processes, alongside a dedicated DM decay module in AREPO-2. We validate the implementations through beam-lattice deflection, thermalization and decay tests, isolated-halo gravothermal core-collapse simulations, and cosmological box and zoom-in simulations. The results recover analytical predictions and published benchmarks and demonstrate agreement across numerical schemes. Our theory-to-simulation framework serves as a cross-disciplinary reference and a practical bridge between SIDM particle physics and simulations of nonlinear structure formation.
item.dc:creator: Martin Rosenlyst, Vinh Tran, Oliver Zier, Xuejian Shen, Mark Vogelsberger, Thejs Brinckmann, Mads T. Frandsen, Jes\'us Zavala, Frederik Holt Dihver Christensen, Mikkel Theiss Kristensen

item.title: Rapid Graviton Thermalization through a Scalar--Gauss--Bonnet Coupling
item.description: arXiv:2610.20325v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that gravitons can thermalize much faster than the universe expands in an effective scalar-mediated model. A thermal fermion bath maintains a massive scalar close to equilibrium, while scalar decay and inverse decay, $\phi\rightleftarrows g+g$, drive the graviton distribution toward a Bose--Einstein distribution with zero chemical potential. We establish this equilibrium state and calculate how it is reached from an initially empty graviton sector. For a scalar mass of $1\,{\rm TeV}$, an interaction scale $\Lambda_{\rm int}=m_\phi/0.03$, and a Yukawa coupling $y=0.03$, the graviton occupations approach their equilibrium values to within $0.1\%$ over $0.1\leq p/T\leq5$ after approximately $0.024$ initial Hubble times, including cosmic expansion and energy transfer from the bath. This interval contains the thermal energy-spectrum peak. The scalar remains close to equilibrium, its vacuum decay widths are narrow, and the graviton interaction is perturbative over the reaction domain. Assuming the effective theory applies on this domain, our results demonstrate that gravitons can reach near-thermal equilibrium under these conditions. We also derive the present-day thermal spectrum for a specified decoupling and entropy history.
item.dc:creator: Hongguang Zhang, Zhengyang Qiu, Sirui Wang, Jiayi Wei

item.title: MadStree: automated evaluation of tree-level de Sitter correlators
item.description: arXiv:2610.28526v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We first derived the formulae of recursive reduction and d log-form differential equations for arbitrary tree-level and loop-integrand cosmological correlators, taking the external relations of massless bulk propagators into consideration. The differential equations could be systematically solved and provide the efficient evaluation of them. We have implemented this methodology as a Mathematica package MadStree. To demonstrate the efficiency of our method, we evaluated up to $10^6$ points for each master integral in our examples, and found that the average computational cost per numerical point per master integral is on the order of $\mu\mathrm{s}$.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Chen, Yi-Xiao Tao, Xinyi Wang, Dong Zhang

item.title: Massive Scalar Quasinormal Modes and Quasibound States of Charged Black Holes with Logarithmic corrections
item.description: arXiv:2610.33883v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study how long-range deformations in a black-hole metric affect the oscillation, trapping, and decay of a neutral, minimally coupled massive scalar field. We choose a logarithmic deformation of Reissner-Nordstr\"om (RN) sourced by nonlinear electrodynamics, arising as an exact solution of Einstein gravity. The same geometry also arises in a phenomenological perfect-fluid dark-matter model. We provide several exact completions of this geometry with finite Arnowitt-Deser-Misner (ADM) mass. Focusing on the original logarithmic geometry, we analyze both quasinormal modes (QNMs), which describe relaxation, and quasibound states (QBSs), which describe trapped modes with small horizon absorption. We first show that a small scalar mass moves the potential barrier outward, raises it, and reduces its curvature. First-order WKB then predicts weaker damping at every fixed finite multipole and overtone. We then compare several approaches, namely sixth-order WKB, global matching, a generalized Leaver method (adapted to the logarithmic geometry) and time-domain evolution. All methods yield consistent QNM estimates within their ranges of validity. Global matching and Leaver also agree closely for QBSs. Further analytic estimates with a reference trapped state show that a local Pad\'e approximation gives a binding-energy error of about $0.04\%$, while leading Gamow tunnelling underestimates damping by about $25\%$. Across the sampled QBSs, increasing the scalar mass or nonlinear coupling strengthens binding but shortens the lifetime through greater horizon absorption. Finally, using an appropriate horizon regularization and a common complex radial contour, we demonstrate orthogonality of an independently computed QNM-QBS pair using a suitable relativistic bilinear framework.
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Paul, Rickmoy Samanta

item.title: Particle dynamics in rotating charged Bumblebee black holes: An analytical correspondence with Kerr-Newman
item.description: arXiv:2611.04750v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish an analytical correspondence between the equatorial dynamics of spinless and spinning test particles in a slowly rotating charged Einstein--Bumblebee black hole spacetime and those in an effective Kerr--Newman spacetime. For spinning particles, the correspondence is established within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework under appropriate parameter matching. We show that corresponding circular orbits have identical radii and coordinate angular velocities, while their radial dynamics and local instability rates exhibit a Lorentz-violation-dependent scaling. Nevertheless, the correspondence does not imply complete dynamical equivalence, as orbital trajectories and radial perturbation growth over an azimuthal period generally differ. These results delineate the scope and limitations of the effective Kerr--Newman correspondence by distinguishing the dynamical properties preserved under parameter matching from those modified by the Lorentz-violating radial deformation.
item.dc:creator: Deyou Chen, Chuang Yang
